Nether
NETH-er
adjective
From the Old English neoþera, “lower, further down,” comparative of niþer, “down”; hence lower, under, beneath — as the nether millstone lies under the upper.

Biblical Definition

Nether means lower — the under one, the thing beneath. The KJV uses it in three places, and each is worth knowing. It marks the foot of Sinai: “Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet with God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount” (Exo 19:17). The people met God at the bottom, under bounds, while the mountain smoked above them — nearness on God’s terms, not man’s. It marks a mercy in the law of pledges: “No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge: for he taketh a man’s life to pledge” (Deu 24:6). The nether millstone was the great fixed stone on which the upper turned; take either and the family cannot grind, and a creditor who seizes the mill has seized the bread. And it marks the place of the dead: Ezekiel’s dirge over the tall tree brings the proud down “to the nether parts of the earth” (Eze 31:16), to lie among the uncircumcised with them that be slain by the sword (Eze 31:18). The word therefore teaches direction. Man’s instinct is upward — the tower, the tall tree, the top among the thick boughs. God’s answer to every such height is the nether parts of the earth; and His way up is down, for the Lord who descended is the same also that ascended far above all heavens.

Webster 1828 Definition

Lower; under; lying beneath — as the nether millstone under the upper, the nether part of the mount, the nether parts of the earth.

NETHER, lower; lying beneath or under; opposed to upper.

From the Saxon neoþera, “lower,” from niþer, “down.”

The nether millstone is the fixed stone on which the upper turns (Deu 24:6).

Israel stood at the nether part of the mount to meet with God (Exo 19:17).

The nether parts of the earth are the place of the dead (Eze 31:16).

Key Scripture

Exo 19:17 — "And Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet with God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount."

Deu 24:6 — "No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge: for he taketh a man's life to pledge."

Eze 31:16 — "I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell with them that descend into the pit: and all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth."

Eze 31:18 — "To whom art thou thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? yet shalt thou be brought down with the trees of Eden unto the nether parts of the earth: thou shalt lie in the midst of the uncircumcised with them that be slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, saith the Lord GOD."

Modern Corruption

Not a contested doctrine but the plain old word for lower; it recovers that God brings every proud height down to the nether parts, and that His way up is down.

expand to see more

The word rebukes the creditor who forgets he is dealing with a life. God legislated the nether millstone: no man shall take the nether or the upper to pledge, for he taketh a man’s life to pledge. A mill is not furniture; it is the household’s bread, and a lender who carries off either stone has not secured a debt, he has stopped a family’s eating. The LORD writes that into His law and gives the reason, so that no man can plead the letter of a contract against the life of his neighbour. There is a whole doctrine of lending in one clause: a debt may be collected, but never out of the means by which the debtor lives.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the direction God has fixed for pride. Ezekiel’s tall tree shot up his top among the thick boughs and was fair in his greatness, and every tree of Eden envied him — and the LORD brought him down to the nether parts of the earth, to lie with the uncircumcised and them that be slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh, says the prophet; and it is Babel’s tower, and every height men raise for themselves. But mark the opposite motion in the gospel: Israel met God at the nether part of the mount, at the bottom, under bounds, because sinners cannot climb to Him — and Christ came down to the nether parts Himself, that He might raise His people up. Whoso exalteth himself shall be abased, and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means lower, under, lying beneath — the opposite of upper.

expand to see more

Nether — Old English neoþera, “lower, further down.”

From niþer, “down”; it is the comparative of downward.

The nether millstone is the fixed stone under the turning upper (Deu 24:6).

The nether part of the mount is its foot, where Israel stood (Exo 19:17).

The nether parts of the earth are the pit, the place of the dead (Eze 31:16).

Usage

"No man shall take the nether millstone to pledge: he taketh a man’s life to pledge."

"Israel stood at the nether part of the mount — near to God, but under bounds He set."

"The tall tree of Eden was brought down to the nether parts: God’s answer to every height."
